images.title: Stamp-resist-dyed cotton, probably Ahmadabad
images.caption: A block-stamped resist-dyed cotton, probably from Ahmadabad, with a pattern reserved in white against a deep blue ground. Gujarat's resist-dyed cottons were traded across the Indian Ocean in the era when Portuguese ships reached India by the Cape route (1498).
images.creator: Unknown maker, India (Gujarat)
images.creditLine: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Gift of Nelly, Violet and Elie Abemayor, in memory of Michel Abemayor, 1978 (CC0)

images.title: Bed hanging, blue-resist textile
images.caption: A cotton bed hanging patterned by painted and block-printed resist and dyed deep blue. The Met catalogues it as an Indian textile made for the American market; blue-resist cottons furnished colonial homes in the decades when Carolina became an indigo exporter.
images.creator: Unknown maker
images.creditLine: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Gift of Mrs. Reginald P. Rose and Franklin Benkard, 1954 (CC0)
images.locationNote: Used in colonial America; place of manufacture per the Met is India (coordinates: New York, representative)
images.rightsEvidence: Met Collection API /public/collection/v1/objects/13561 returns "isPublicDomain": true (Met Open Access, CC0). Accession 54.59.1; credit "Gift of Mrs. Reginald P. Rose and Franklin Benkard, 1954".

images.title: Loom width with stylized leaf design
images.caption: Hot wax was stamped onto the cotton with carved woodblocks, the cloth dyed in indigo, then boiled to melt away the wax and reveal the pattern, as the Cleveland Museum of Art describes. French printed-cotton makers drew on Indian textile designs.
images.creator: Unknown maker, France
images.creditLine: Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of Gertrude Underhill (CC0)
images.locationNote: Museum lists 'France, Alsace, Sain-Bel'; coordinates: Mulhouse (representative)
images.rightsEvidence: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access API /api/artworks/114934 returns "share_license_status": "CC0" (accession 1935.113; credit "Gift of Gertrude Underhill").

images.title: Dye House at Konya-chō, Kanda
images.caption: From Hiroshige's One Hundred Famous Views of Edo: long lengths of blue-and-white dyed cloth hang from drying towers in Konya-chō, Edo's dyers' district, with Mount Fuji beyond.
images.creator: Utagawa Hiroshige

images.title: Adire eleko panel with George V and Queen Mary
images.caption: Yoruba adire eleko is made by painting or stencilling a cassava-starch resist onto cotton before dyeing it in indigo. This panel with portraits of George V and Queen Mary (reigned 1910–36) was shown in the 'Indigo Blue' exhibition at Gawthorpe Hall, Lancashire.
images.creator: Unknown Yoruba artist; photograph by Michael Garlick

images.title: Indigo vat, Blaudruckerei Wagner
images.caption: The indigo vat at the Wagner hand-blueprinting workshop in Bad Leonfelden, Upper Austria. Blaudruck – resist block printing and indigo dyeing – was inscribed on UNESCO's intangible cultural heritage list in 2018 for Austria, Czechia, Germany, Hungary and Slovakia.
